relations.myth: Golden statues during the plague of 180 BCE
relations.note: Golden statues of Apollo, Aesculapius, and Salus were ordered during an epidemic.
Terence invokes Aesculapius and Salus together on behalf of a person's health.

relations.myth: Golden statues during the plague of 180 BCE
relations.note: Golden statues of Aesculapius, Apollo, and Salus were ordered during an epidemic.
Greek translation and serpent-feeding imagery gradually identified Salus with Hygieia.
Salus and Valetudo occupy opposite coin faces, associating but possibly distinguishing civic safety and bodily health.
Ovid places Janus and Roman Salus within the same calendrical observance.
Ovid places Concordia and Roman Salus within the same calendrical observance.
Imperial Arval ceremonies associated Salus with Concordia through rites performed in Concordia's temple.
Ovid places Roman Salus beside the Ara Pacis in an Augustan observance.
Arval records place Salus Publica after Jupiter in annual vows for emperor and state.
Salus's annual vow was formulated by reference to the vow made to Juno.
Salus follows Minerva and the other Capitoline gods in sacrificial prescriptions.

relations.myth: Imperial coinage linking salvation and victory
relations.note: Coin programs associate Salus and Victoria to present public rescue as achieved through victory.

relations.myth: Imperial coinage linking safety, fortune, and return
relations.note: Imperial issues linked Salus Generis Humani with victorious fortune and safe return.
Coin programs coordinated Mars's vengeance on the tyrant with Salus's promise of public salvation.
The Senate coordinated honors to Sol with a proposed temple to Salus after Nero survived conspiracy.
Scholars hypothesized a relationship through Salus's isolated late title Semonia; no divine interaction is attested.
A dedication to Hercules follows the same cultic rules as an altar of Salus.
